A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe the same JOSH/JOSH3R research. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the research text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are unchanged and available for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original reconstruction experiments on SLOPER4D, EMDB, and RICH, JOSH3R training results, ablations, and robustness experiments in Section 4 and Appendices C–F.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the same original benchmark results, JOSH3R experiments, ablations, and robustness results, including Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix H retain identical JOSH initialization, contact losses, joint optimization, focal-length adjustment, and JOSH3R architecture and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SLOPER4D, EMDB, and RICH coverage, web-video training data, qualitative scenarios, and noisy-initialization evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments. Both retain SynCHMR* in Table 1, the same human-motion and scene-reconstruction baselines in Tables 3–6, and the same training comparisons in Figure 7.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices B–H specify identical sequence selections, alignment procedures, metrics, training settings, and testing protocols. The exclusion of SLOPER4D seq009 from scene evaluation is retained.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same contact-loss, human-parameter optimization, and camera-intrinsics ablations. Appendix F and Table 7 retain identical perturbation experiments for depth, contact labels, and human initialization.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results in Tables 1–7 and the figures are unchanged. For example, Table 6 reports the same JOSH3 EMDB errors of 68.9 WA-MPJPE and 174.7 W-MPJPE in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, reconstruction and loss formulations, and transformation equations in Sections 2–3, including Equations 1–9, are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about joint human-scene reconstruction, improved reconstruction accuracy, and scalable JOSH3R training using JOSH-generated web-video labels.

C2.justification: The interpretations of joint optimization, robustness, and JOSH3R's accuracy–speed tradeoff are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning poor initialization and unavailable or ambiguous human-scene contacts.

D1.justification: Appendices B, G, and H retain identical hyperparameters, optimization budgets, hardware, data-processing instructions, and training details. The project link and code-release statements are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography, related-work discussion in Appendix A, and positioning against prior research are identical. The added funding acknowledgment introduces no research citation or novelty claim.

P1.justification: Page 11 changes 'supported by' to 'supported in part by' and adds NSF grant GCR-2524088. Page 1 updates the arXiv version/date stamp. All other prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–7 retain identical content, formatting, captions, and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the acknowledgment edit only rewraps text within its existing two-line block.

improvement.justification: v3.pdf adds a funding credit and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. These administrative edits leave the scientific content, empirical support, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation unchanged, including all appendices, so they do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
